title: AML / Reporting Thresholds

sections.heading: Money Laundering — Definition & 3 Stages
items: Money laundering = converting illicit proceeds into apparently legitimate funds.
Stage 1 — PLACEMENT: cash enters the financial system (deposits, money orders, chips). Highest detection risk.
Stage 2 — LAYERING: separate funds from source via complex transactions (wires, securities trades, shell co's, offshore).
Stage 3 — INTEGRATION: funds re-enter economy looking legitimate (real estate, business, luxury goods).
Reverse money laundering / terrorist financing = clean money funding illegal activity (still SAR-reportable).

items.Trigger: Cash in/out > $10,000 single day (aggregated, same customer)
Suspicious activity ≥ $5,000 (where suspect identified or identifiable)
items.Deadline: 30 days from detection; +30 days (60 total) if no suspect ID'd
items.Applies To: Any suspicious txn; confidential — do NOT tell customer

sections.heading: Structuring (Smurfing)
items: Structuring = breaking cash into amounts < $10,000 to evade CTR (e.g., 3 deposits of $4,000 same day).
ILLEGAL regardless of source of funds — triggers SAR.
Aggregation rule: multiple same-day cash txns by/for same person are summed for CTR.

sections.heading: AML Program — FINRA Rule 3310 (5 Required Elements)
items: 1. Written policies & procedures reasonably designed to detect/report suspicious activity.
2. Designated AML Compliance Officer (AMLCO) — name reported to FINRA.
3. Ongoing employee training.
4. Independent annual testing (every calendar year; every 2 yrs if no customer-facing biz).
5. CIP — Customer Identification Program (USA PATRIOT Act §326): name, DOB, address, TIN/SSN before account opens.
USA PATRIOT Act §352 — required AML program; §314(a) law-enforcement info requests; §314(b) voluntary info-sharing between FIs.

sections.heading: OFAC & SDN List
items: OFAC = Office of Foreign Assets Control (U.S. Treasury) — administers economic sanctions.
SDN List = Specially Designated Nationals & Blocked Persons (terrorists, narco-traffickers, sanctioned regimes).
Firm must screen new and existing customers against SDN list.
Match → BLOCK/FREEZE assets immediately, REJECT transaction, report to OFAC (not just SAR).
Strict liability — no knowledge requirement; penalties even for inadvertent violations.

sections.heading: FINRA Rule 3220 — Gifts & Gratuities
items: Limit: $100 per person per year (aggregate) for gifts in relation to the business of the recipient's employer.
Excluded: personal gifts (e.g., wedding), de minimis promotional items (logo pens, etc.), business entertainment (must be reasonable & both parties present).
Records of all gifts must be retained.
Related: Rule 3240 (borrowing/lending w/ customers — generally prohibited), Rule 3210 (outside accounts), Rule 3250 (no conditions on non-cash comp).

items.Role: Receives CTRs & SARs; admin of BSA

sections.heading: Recordkeeping (cross-ref)
items: SARs and supporting docs: retain 5 years from filing (BSA).
CTRs: retain 5 years.
AML records generally under 17 CFR 240.17a-4 retention regimes.

common_traps: CTR is CASH only and > $10,000 — wires, checks, and ACH do NOT trigger a CTR (they may trigger a SAR).
SAR threshold is $5,000 (not $10,000) and the filing deadline is 30 days (60 if no suspect). Never tip off the customer — disclosure of a SAR is a federal crime.
Stages order: PLACEMENT → LAYERING → INTEGRATION. Exam often lists 'structuring' as a stage — structuring is a TECHNIQUE used in placement, not one of the three stages.
Rule 3220 gift limit is $100/person/YEAR aggregate — not per gift. Business entertainment (meals, events with rep present) is NOT counted toward the $100 cap.
OFAC hit = BLOCK/FREEZE and report to OFAC; it is separate from (and in addition to) any SAR filing. Strict liability — intent doesn't matter.
